attempted_claim: For untwisted affine root systems of classical types B_n^{(1)} and C_n^{(1)}, with nonsymmetric E_lambda(q,t) and symmetric P_lambda(q,t) normalized as in Ion, and E_lambda(q,infinity), P_lambda(q,infinity) defined by Ion's renormalized t^{-1}=0 limit (all t_i to infinity after multiplying by product (1-q^{-(alpha_{j_i},lambda^{(i)})}) along a reduced alcove chain), decide the exact finite-q statement: for every anti-dominant weight lambda, does P_lambda(q,infinity) = sum_{mu <= lambda} d_{lambda mu}(q) chi_mu hold with d_{lambda mu}(q) in N[q^{-1}], d_{lambda lambda}=1, where chi_mu is the finite Weyl character, and what is the explicit degenerated affine DAHA intertwiner at t=infinity that governs E_lambda(q,infinity) in place of the affine Demazure operator Delta_0 when Ion's identity E_lambda(q,infinity)=q^{(Lambda_0,w_lambda tilde lambda)} chi(E_{w_lambda}(tilde lambda)) fails?
decisive_failure: The investigation could not resolve the affine Demazure-Lusztig operator T0 normalization: every candidate variant failed the exact Hecke quadratic guardrail while finite T1 passed it, so no validated C2/B2 nonsymmetric computation, t=infinity limit, Weyl-character expansion, or degenerated intertwiner formula was obtained. Literature pinpointing and the C2 reduced-word enumeration remain unverified intermediates, not substitutes for the target theorem.
